citation: Hart, H., Young, C., Chen, A., Zou, A., & Allensworth, E.M. (2020). Supporting school improvement: Early findings from reexamination of the 5Essentials survey. Chicago, IL: University of Chicago Consortium on School Research. https://www.5-essentials.org/
title: 5Essentials Survey: 22 Rasch-scored measures of school organization for teachers and students
description: The 5Essentials Survey captures the strength of each essential support through items completed by teachers and students; underlying concepts such as Instructional Leadership or Student-Teacher Trust are captured with groups of items called measures. Each survey includes 20 measures, with 22 unique measures across levels. Measures were recalibrated with Rasch analysis on 2014–19 data, and respondent Rasch scores were weighted by precision to compute school-level mean scores. The survey has been administered in more than 6,000 schools and since 2014 counts for 5–10 percent of a CPS school's quality rating.
requirements: Measures must maintain acceptable Rasch reliability and explain sufficient variance at the school level to differentiate schools
constraints: Because school ratings are consequential, the report notes there could be pressure for schools to appear strong, and exaggerated responses would compromise the survey's ability to accurately assess performance
Fourth- and fifth-grade students fully participated for the first time in 2020 and were not included in the analyses
target_learning_goals: Measuring school organizational strength to guide improvement in student outcomes
examples: In 2014 the survey became part of CPS accountability policy, comprising 5–10 percent of a school's quality rating; results reports have been publicly available since 2013
key_sources: Hart, H., Young, C., Chen, A., Zou, A., & Allensworth, E.M. (2020). Supporting school improvement: Early findings from reexamination of the 5Essentials survey. Chicago, IL: University of Chicago Consortium on School Research. https://consortium.uchicago.edu/publications/supporting-school-improvement

article_title: Next Generation Science Standards in Practice: Tools and Processes Used by the California NGSS Early Implementers
citation: Tyler, B., & DiRanna, K. (2018). Next Generation Science Standards in practice: Tools and processes used by the California NGSS Early Implementers. San Francisco, CA: WestEd. https://www.wested.org
title: 5E instructional model (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate) for developing NGSS learning sequences
description: The 5E instructional model, originally developed by BSCS (Bybee et al., 2006), is used by Early Implementers to develop learning sequences of multiple lessons, each based on an investigative phenomenon from the conceptual flow. It is "based on the constructivist approach to learning, which says that learners build new ideas on top of prior knowledge and understanding", and its five stages move from capturing interest and eliciting prior knowledge through exploration, student explanation, application, and evaluation occurring throughout the cycle. Teachers plan each stage with a backwards design recording the 3D concepts, what the teacher does, and what the student does.
requirements: Planning driven by student questioning, experience, and discussion; each stage records a three-dimensional concept including specific DCIs, SEPs, and CCCs
constraints: Because NGSS calls for 3D instruction, a learning sequence is seldom completed in a single class period
target_learners: K-8 students in Early Implementer districts
target_learning_goals: Student-centered, inquiry-based science lessons building deep conceptual understanding rather than memory of facts
examples: Nine grade K-8 NGSS Early Implementer Learning Sequences were created and field tested, such as Kindergarten Pushes and Pulls, 5th Grade What's in Your Water?, and 8th Grade Understanding White Sharks
key_sources: Tyler, B., & DiRanna, K. (2018). Next Generation Science Standards in practice: Tools and processes used by the California NGSS Early Implementers. San Francisco, CA: WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED596757

article_title: Design mobile computational thinking-integrated mathematics lessons based on the 5E instructional model for primary students
citation: Fang, X., Ng, D. T. K., Tam, W. T., & Yuen, M. (2025). Design mobile computational thinking-integrated mathematics lessons based on the 5E instructional model for primary students. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10513-x
title: 5E instructional model structuring mobile app development mathematics lessons in five stages
description: The article uses the 5E instructional model (engagement, exploration, explanation, elaboration, evaluation) as the instructional design framework for mobile CT-integrated mathematics lessons. Each stage maps to app development activities: engagement reviews prior area knowledge and arouses interest in calculation games; exploration has students design game interfaces on paper; explanation asks students to explain designs; elaboration extends to complex cases like null values; evaluation involves testing games and reflecting. The article states the model 'could be suitable for the instructional design of primary school CT-integrated mathematics curriculum.'
requirements: A teacher able to guide app development activities across all five stages
A mobile app development platform such as App Inventor
constraints: Studied with primary five students in Hong Kong on the topic of area
examples: Two 2-hour lessons: 1 hour instruction and 1 hour hands-on paper prototyping and programming activities
key_sources: Fang, X., Ng, D. T. K., Tam, W. T., & Yuen, M. (2025). Design mobile computational thinking-integrated mathematics lessons based on the 5E instructional model for primary students. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-025-10513-x

article_title: A Comparative Meta-Analysis of 5E and Traditional Approaches in Turkey
citation: Özgür Anil, Veli Batdi. (2015). A Comparative Meta-Analysis of 5E and Traditional Approaches in Turkey. Journal of Education and Training Studies. https://doi.org/10.11114/jets.v3i6.1038
title: Meta-analytic corpus of 14 Turkish 5E studies (2008-2014) analysed with CMA and MetaWin
description: A corpus of studies and theses on the 5E instructional model published in Turkey between 2008 and 2014, screened from 161 accessed publications (118 articles and 43 theses) down to 14 included studies. The article states "a review undertaken of the studies and theses (N=14) executed in Turkey over the period 2008-2014 on the 5E model", with academic achievement N:13, retention N:5 and attitude N:8. Effect sizes were computed as Hedges' d using the Comprehensive Meta-Analysis (CMA) program, MetaWin and Microsoft Excel 2010, and intercoder reliability between two encoders was calculated as 100%.
requirements: Studies had to contain statistical values such as sample size, arithmetic means and standard deviations, and use a pretest-posttest and control group model
constraints: Some studies were excluded because they did not reflect the relevant nature of experimental research
target_learners: students in Turkish schools and universities taught with the 5E model
examples: The article reports 336, 149 and 225 students in experimental groups for achievement, retention and attitude respectively, with control group sizes of 324, 137 and 211
key_sources: Özgür Anil, Veli Batdi. (2015). A Comparative Meta-Analysis of 5E and Traditional Approaches in Turkey. Journal of Education and Training Studies. https://doi.org/10.11114/jets.v3i6.1038

article_title: A Comparative Meta-Analysis of 5E and Traditional Approaches in Turkey
citation: Özgür Anil, Veli Batdi. (2015). A Comparative Meta-Analysis of 5E and Traditional Approaches in Turkey. Journal of Education and Training Studies. https://doi.org/10.11114/jets.v3i6.1038
title: The 5E instructional model as a five-stage constructivist learning cycle
description: The 5E instructional model, developed by Bybee at the Biological Science Curriculum Study, is a constructivist teaching sequence grounded in the view that knowledge is constructed by the individual rather than passively transmitted. The article states "This model is based on 5 different stages of learning: Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate and Evaluate." In this model the student plays an active role, the teacher acts as a guide, and learning is focused on process rather than product, associating the learning environment with the world outside the classroom. The meta-analysis treats this model as the intervention whose effects on achievement, retention and attitude are pooled across studies.
requirements: Instruction designed within the model engages students at every stage so they make their own conceptualizations
constraints: The article reports that teachers needed more time for classroom preparation in order to implement the 5E instructional model
target_learners: school and university students in science and other subjects
examples: Studies in the corpus applied the model across subjects including physics, biology, geography, mathematics and social studies
key_sources: Özgür Anil, Veli Batdi. (2015). A Comparative Meta-Analysis of 5E and Traditional Approaches in Turkey. Journal of Education and Training Studies. https://doi.org/10.11114/jets.v3i6.1038

article_title: Effect of 5E Learning Model on Academic Achievement, Attitude and Science Process Skills: Meta-Analysis Study
citation: Nevin Kozcu Cakır. (2017). Effect of 5E Learning Model on Academic Achievement, Attitude and Science Process Skills: Meta-analysis Study. Journal of Education and Training Studies, 5(11). https://doi.org/10.11114/jets.v5i11.2649
title: The 5E learning model: a five-phase constructivist instructional sequence for science courses
description: The 5E learning model is a constructivist instructional model for science courses comprising five phases: introduction (engagement), discovery (exploration), description (explanation), expanding (elaboration), and assessment (evaluation). The article describes it as a way "to design science courses based on structural approach and cognitive psychology" (Bybee, 1997), in which prior knowledge is identified, a research question is posed, first-hand experience is gained under teacher guidance, and the concept is transferred to a new field and evaluated.
requirements: Studies applying the model in the synthesized corpus used it in the experimental group while the control group received traditional teaching
constraints: The article's synthesis is limited to studies applied in science and technology courses in Turkey between 2006 and 2016 with semi-experimental designs
target_learners: university students and pre-service teachers in science courses
examples: The article describes each phase, e.g. in the introduction step "a short demonstration, problem situation or event is given in order to evaluate and reveal the preliminary knowledge of students".

article_title: The Effects of 5E Inquiry Learning Activities on Achievement and Attitude toward Chemistry
citation: Senol Sen & Ozge Ozyalcin Oskay. (2016). The Effects of 5E Inquiry Learning Activities on Achievement and Attitude toward Chemistry. Journal of Education and Learning, 6(1). https://doi.org/10.5539/jel.v6n1p1
title: The 5E learning cycle model: engagement, exploration, explanation, elaboration, evaluation
description: The 5E learning model is an inquiry-based instructional model composed of five sequential stages: "engagement, exploration, explanation, elaboration and evaluation". Engagement activates prior knowledge and arouses curiosity; exploration has students researching answers through hands-on activities; explanation has teachers help students connect their explanations with scientific knowledge and address misconceptions; elaboration has students apply knowledge to new situations; evaluation checks targeted gains using complementary measurement throughout the process. The study implemented this model over five weeks for teaching factors affecting chemical equilibrium.
requirements: Teachers act as guides and facilitators rather than sources of correct answers, leading with questions
constraints: The article notes the engagement stage is described as the most important stage of the model
examples: Students worked in pairs or groups of three, generated research questions, ran experiments on factors affecting chemical equilibrium, and evaluated their own learning in end-of-experiment reports
key_sources: Senol Sen & Ozge Ozyalcin Oskay. (2016). The Effects of 5E Inquiry Learning Activities on Achievement and Attitude toward Chemistry. Journal of Education and Learning, 6(1). https://doi.org/10.5539/jel.v6n1p1

article_title: In Search of a More Effective Strategy: Using the 5E Instructional Strategy to Teach Civic Education in Senior Secondary Schools in Ilorin, Nigeria
citation: AbdulRaheem, Y., Bello, M. B., & Odutayo, A. O. (2018). In Search of a More Effective Strategy: Using the 5E Instructional Strategy to Teach Civic Education in Senior Secondary Schools in Ilorin, Nigeria. Journal of International Social Studies, 8(1), 62-85. http://www.iajiss.org
title: 5E instructional strategy: a five-phase constructivist learning cycle (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate)
description: The 5Es instructional strategy is a learning-cycle model developed in the 1980s that encourages a constructivist approach while introducing aspects of behaviorism and cognitivism. Each stage describes a phase of learning: "Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, and Evaluate". Engage captures attention and activates prior knowledge; Explore provides a common concrete learning experience with active exploration; Explain introduces common terms in a more teacher-directed phase; Elaborate extends concepts to new situations in increasing order of difficulty; Evaluate involves both formal and informal assessment. The article applies it to Civic Education, a non-science subject.
requirements: Commences with students' current knowledge and makes connections between current and new knowledge
Provides direct instruction of ideas students could not learn on their own and opportunities to demonstrate understanding
Adequate instructional materials
constraints: The article notes a belief that the 5Es strategy is meant for teaching only science-based subjects, which this study tests in an arts/social science subject
target_learners: students of all ages, including adults
target_learning_goals: generic skills and autonomous learning capabilities
examples: In this study, an intact class of 39 Senior School II students was taught Civic Education through the 5Es phases while a conventional class of 38 served as control
key_sources: AbdulRaheem, Y., Bello, M. B., & Odutayo, A. O. (2018). article_title: The 5E Instructional Model: A Constructivist Approach for Enhancing Students' Learning Outcomes in Mathematics
citation: Stephen Akinyemi Omotayo & Joshua Oluwatoyin Adeleke. (2017). The 5E Instructional Model: A Constructivist Approach for Enhancing Students' Learning Outcomes in Mathematics. JISTE, Vol. 21, No. 2, 2017.
title: The 5E instructional model: a constructivist five-phase learning cycle
description: The 5E instructional model organizes teaching into five phases — Engagement, Exploration, Explanation, Elaboration, and Evaluation — each with stated aims, teacher roles, and activity examples. It is "derived from the Atkin and Karplus learning cycle" incorporated into the SCIS program, with engagement and evaluation added by BSCS. The article describes it as an approach that "maximizes opportunities for learner participation by engaging them with a series of activities that assist them to construct their own understanding," with teachers acting as facilitators.
requirements: Teachers must be trained in the model; in the study teachers received a two-week training with micro teaching to ensure mastery of the teaching method
constraints: The article notes a constructivist-based instructional approach, if not adequately utilized and implemented by a well-trained teacher, may not yield the desired result
target_learners: senior secondary school II mathematics students (average age 15)
target_learning_goals: constructing conceptual understanding rather than rote memorization
examples: In the study's instructional guide, the engagement stage lasted 5 minutes and aroused curiosity by asking questions; the exploration stage lasted 20 minutes and used hands-on activities with triangle measurements leading to the Sine rule
key_sources: Stephen Akinyemi Omotayo & Joshua Oluwatoyin Adeleke. (2017). The 5E Instructional Model: A Constructivist Approach for Enhancing Students' Learning Outcomes in Mathematics. JISTE, Vol. 21, No. 2, 2017. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1176946

article_title: The Effect of Inquiry-Based Learning Method on Students' Academic Achievement in Science Course
citation: Ali Abdi. (2014). The Effect of Inquiry-based Learning Method on Students’ Academic Achievement in Science Course. Universal Journal of Educational Research 2(1): 37-41. https://doi.org/10.13189/ujer.2014.020104
title: 5E learning cycle instructional model
description: The 5E learning cycle is an inquiry-based instruction model requiring "the instruction of five discrete elements": Engagement, Exploration, Explanation, Elaboration, and Evaluation. Engagement accesses prior knowledge through curiosity-promoting activities; Exploration provides shared activities in which misconceptions are identified and conceptual change facilitated; Explanation introduces concepts and lets students demonstrate understanding; Elaboration extends concepts to new situations; Evaluation offers formative and summative assessment with feedback. In this study the model structured eight weeks of fifth-grade science teaching.
requirements: Instruction must be organized through all five phases, with activities and lesson plans designed to maximize students' active involvement
constraints: The article applies the model to fifth-grade science units (microbes/disease, nervous system and sense organs, human and environment) with the same textbook and teacher as the comparison group
examples: Lesson plans covered three fifth-grade units; e.g. microbe structure was examined under a microscope in the exploration phase and a research task about the importance of vaccines was given in the elaboration stage

article_title: The Impact of Guiding Materials on Students' Conceptual Understanding: The Case of "What Is the Earth's Crust Composed of?
citation: Tülay Şenel Çoruhlu & Sibel Er Nas. (2017). The Impact of Guidance Materials on Students' Conceptual Understanding: The Case of "What Is the Earth's Crust Composed of?". Journal of Education and Training Studies, 5(2). https://doi.org/10.11114/jets.v5i2.2169
title: 5E-based guidance materials for "What is the Earth's Crust Composed of?" combining case studies, conceptual change texts and worksheets
description: A set of guidance materials developed on the 5E model (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate) for the topic "What is the Earth's Crust Composed of?" in the Turkish 5th-grade science curriculum. The Engage step used a case study entitled "Mines"; the Explore step used a worksheet with a make-a-fossil activity; the Explain step used a conceptual change text entitled "Fossils"; the Elaborate step used a case study entitled "Travertines of Pamukkale are in Danger"; and the Evaluate step used a concept map. The application process was completed within 8 hours of classroom activity, matching the control group's 8 hours with the existing textbook.
requirements: A useful case to be studied should reflect reality and attract the attention of students
Materials were introduced to the teacher by the researchers prior to the intervention
constraints: Applied within the 8 lesson hours provided in the curriculum
Developed for the 5th-grade "Mystery of Earth's Crust" unit
target_learning_goals: Conceptual understanding of rocks, minerals, fossils and natural monuments
examples: The experimental group teacher had 6 years' experience and the control group teacher had 10 years' experience; each teacher completed the application process in 8 lesson hours
key_sources: Tülay Şenel Çoruhlu & Sibel Er Nas. (2017). The Impact of Guidance Materials on Students' Conceptual Understanding: The Case of "What Is the Earth's Crust Composed of?". Journal of Education and Training Studies, 5(2). https://doi.org/10.11114/jets.v5i2.2169

article_title: The Impact of Guiding Materials on Students' Conceptual Understanding: The Case of "What Is the Earth's Crust Composed of?
citation: Tülay Şenel Çoruhlu & Sibel Er Nas. (2017). The Impact of Guidance Materials on Students' Conceptual Understanding: The Case of "What Is the Earth's Crust Composed of?". Journal of Education and Training Studies, 5(2). https://doi.org/10.11114/jets.v5i2.2169
title: The 5E instructional model (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate) as a constructivist framework for designing science guidance materials
description: The 5E model is a constructivist learning-theory-based instructional framework whose phases are Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, and Evaluate. In this study it structured the development of guidance materials: each phase was populated with specific materials (a case study to attract attention in Engage, a worksheet in Explore, a conceptual change text in Explain, another case study in Elaborate, and a concept map in Evaluate). The article situates 5E among models such as 4E and 7E developed in line with the constructivist approach adopted in the science curriculum, and notes the 7E model's perceived complexity in the eyes of teachers.
requirements: Teaching approaches matched to the approach adopted in the curriculum
Teachers need teaching materials to match the approach
constraints: The 7E model variant is perceived as complex by teachers, which motivated the choice of 5E
target_learning_goals: Conceptual understanding of science topics and elimination of misconceptions
examples: The Engage step case study "Mines" aimed to attract the students' attention to the topic; the Evaluate step concept map assessed achievement of the envisaged learning outcomes

article_title: The Effect of Brightness of Lamps Teaching Based on the 5E Model on Students' Academic Achievement and Attitudes
citation: Hatice Guzel. (2016). The effect of brightness of lamps teaching based on the 5E model on students' academic achievement and attitudes. Educational Research and Reviews. https://doi.org/10.5897/ERR2016.2915
title: The 5E learning model as a constructivist science-teaching method with five phases
description: The article describes the 5E model as "a science teaching method which depen ds on research -based constructivist learning theory and experimental activities", developed by Rodger Bybee of BSCS. It consists of five phases — Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate and Evaluate — in which lessons begin with an intriguing problem, students collaboratively generate ideas, teachers provide scientific explanations, students apply learning to new situations, and finally reflect on their understanding. In this study the model was operationalized with worksheets, cartoons, animations, demonstrations and group work.
requirements: Implementation as printed used collaborative student groups, worksheets, and visual materials such as animations and cartoons across the phases
constraints: The author reports it is "quite hard under the conditions of our country to teach all lessons through activities in which the 5E model is used", citing time-consumption and material inadequacy
target_learning_goals: Understanding the brightness of lamps (electric circuits) in grade 11 physics
examples: The experimental group worked in self-chosen groups of two and three for 3 hours weekly over 3 weeks, using worksheets, computer-displayed animations and circuit schemas

title: 5E-model-based collaborative Literature scenario with three literary texts on a wiki platform
description: The didactic intervention was a training scenario divided into three sections representing three different literary texts, based on the 5E Instructional Model (Bybee, 1997) founded on the constructivism-based Atkin and Karplus (1962) model. The five phases are Engagement, Exploration, Explanation, Elaboration and Evaluation, carried out cooperatively with the experimental group working at networked workstations.
requirements: Cooperative teaching method with each group of students having a computer with internet connection in the wiki-supported condition
constraints: The article notes the actual research time was relatively limited, thirteen hours in total, and the subject matter concerned only three literary texts
target_learners: second-grade General Lyceum students studying Modern Greek Literature
examples: Students completed collaboration self-assessment rubrics before and after the scenario, and the teacher rated each group and student with activity assessment rubrics afterwards

article_title: The Effect of the 5E Instructional Model Enriched with Cooperative Learning and Animations on Seventh-Grade Students' Academic Achievement and Scientific Attitudes
citation: İkramettin Daşdemir. (2016). The Effect of the 5E Instructional Model Enriched With Cooperative Learning and Animations on Seventh-Grade Students' Academic Achievement and Scientific Attitudes. International Electronic Journal of Elementary Education, 9(1), 21-38. https://www.iejee.com
title: The 5E instructional model as a five-phase constructivist sequence for science teaching
description: The article describes the 5E instructional model as "The most effective model of constru ctivist learning theory", consisting of five phases: Engage, explore, explain, elaborate, and evaluate. Engage raises curiosity and surfaces students' own ideas; explore has students experiment or investigate with teacher guidance; explain has students describe phenomena while the teacher replaces incomplete knowledge with correct scientific knowledge; elaborate applies new learning to new situations; and evaluate involves teacher observation, questioning, and student self-assessment. The study implemented all three conditions on top of this base model.
requirements: A teacher familiar with the model; the study's teacher had 12 years of experience and experience of teaching with the 5E instructional model
constraints: The study implemented the base 5E model according to the teacher's book within the Turkish secondary science curriculum
target_learning_goals: understanding of the light unit (absorption, refraction, lenses)
examples: The control group received the 5E model alone for 4 weeks (16 hours) on the light unit, with engage-phase questions, explore-phase activities, teacher explanations, application to new situations, and evaluation questioning
key_sources: İkramettin Daşdemir. (2016). The Effect of the 5E Instructional Model Enriched With Cooperative Learning and Animations on Seventh-Grade Students' Academic Achievement and Scientific Attitudes. article_title: The Effects of Animation Supported 5E Model on Teaching "Indicative and Subjunctive Moods" in 7th Grade Turkish Lesson
citation: Mehmet Fatih Özcan, Latife Kirbaşoğlu Kiliç. (2017). The Effects of Animation Supported 5E Model on Teaching 'Indicative and Subjunctive Moods' in 7th Grade Turkish Lesson. Universal Journal of Educational Research. https://doi.org/10.13189/ujer.2017.051407
title: 5E learning model as a five-stage constructivist instructional sequence
description: The article describes the 5E learning model as a classroom adaptation of constructivism comprising five sequential stages: engaging, exploring, explaining, elaborating and evaluating. In the engaging stage the teacher attracts attention and reveals pre-understandings; in exploring, students seek solutions from their own experience; in explaining, students share findings; in elaborating, they apply new concepts to new situations; and in evaluating, students "assess how much they learn new concepts and skills". The study operationalised this model with Flash animations across six weeks of grammar teaching.
requirements: Stages build on prior stages: explanations should relate to experiences of the previous two stages
constraints: Applied in this study to 7th grade Turkish grammar topics (finite/infinite verbs, moods, tenses)
target_learning_goals: Understanding indicative and subjunctive moods and related Turkish grammar topics
examples: The experimental group progressed through the 5E stages week by week with animations: engaging with finite/infinite verbs, exploring moods, explaining tenses, and elaborating with reinforcement activities
key_sources: Mehmet Fatih Özcan, Latife Kirbaşoğlu Kiliç. (2017). The Effects of Animation Supported 5E Model on Teaching 'Indicative and Subjunctive Moods' in 7th Grade Turkish Lesson. Universal Journal of Educational Research. https://doi.org/10.13189/ujer.2017.051407

article_title: Effectiveness of a "5E+AI" teaching model on science communication in medical students: a contribution to global health literacy.
citation: Dai Huiru, Liu Minling, Li Tingwei, Wang Jiancheng, Fang Shuo. (2026). Effectiveness of a “5E+AI” teaching model on science communication in medical students: a contribution to global health literacy. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1916714
title: The 5E+AI instructional model: the 5E cycle as organizational framework with generative AI supporting content generation, simulation-based training, and feedback optimization
description: The 5E+AI model uses the 5E instructional model (Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate) as the "organizational framework, with generative AI tools serving as assistive technologies covering three task types: content generation, simulation-based training, and feedback optimization." AI supports learning through "on-demand information retrieval, simulated practice partners, and automated personalized feedback at each phase of the 5E cycle." The model was implemented in a 12-week medical science communication course for clinical medicine undergraduates.
requirements: Requires generative AI tools integrated as a core component across all five 5E phases, not used as a standalone tool
constraints: Evaluated in a single elective course at one institution with limited enrollment per semester
key_sources: Dai Huiru, Liu Minling, Li Tingwei, Wang Jiancheng, Fang Shuo. (2026). Effectiveness of a “5E+AI” teaching model on science communication in medical students: a contribution to global health literacy. Frontiers in Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1916714

article_title: Improvements from a flipped classroom may simply be the fruits of active learning.
citation: Jensen Jamie L., Kummer Tyler A., Godoy Patricia D. d. M. (2015). Improvements from a Flipped Classroom May Simply Be the Fruits of Active Learning. CBE—Life Sciences Education. https://doi.org/10.1187/cbe.14-08-0129
title: 5-E learning cycle (engage, explore, explain, elaborate, evaluate)
description: The 5-E learning cycle is a constructivist instructional model with five phases: "Engage serves to interest the students in the material and engage them in the process of learning"; Explore lets students construct understanding before terminology; Explain introduces terms; Elaborate applies concepts to novel situations; Evaluate assesses formatively and summatively. The first three phases serve content attainment and elaborate serves concept application. The study used it in both flipped and nonflipped conditions.
requirements: Instructor or materials must facilitate both a content attainment phase and a concept application phase, with one phase delegated to out-of-class work due to classroom time constraints
target_learning_goals: application of concepts to novel situations
examples: In both study conditions, engage/explore took the form of group or video-guided exploration of a puzzling biological phenomenon, explain was a minilecture, and elaborate was higher-order problem solving
key_sources: Jensen Jamie L., Kummer Tyler A., Godoy Patricia D. d. M. (2015). Improvements from a Flipped Classroom May Simply Be the Fruits of Active Learning. CBE—Life Sciences Education. https://doi.org/10.1187/cbe.14-08-0129
